australia/sydney-opera-house.name: Sydney Opera House
australia/sydney-opera-house.description: The sail-roofed performing arts centre on Sydney Harbour, visited on a tour or for an evening show.
australia/sydney-opera-house.details: The Opera House is the most recognisable building in Australia. Guided tours go behind the scenes, and evening concerts, opera and ballet make good use of the setting. The forecourt and Circular Quay promenade are free to wander and give the classic harbour views. Book show seats ahead.

australia/harbour-bridge-climb.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge climb
australia/harbour-bridge-climb.description: A guided climb over the arch of the bridge, or a walk up to the pylon lookout.
australia/harbour-bridge-climb.details: The BridgeClimb takes small groups up the arch for panoramic views of the harbour and Opera House, lasting about three hours. A less demanding option is the Pylon Lookout on the bridge, reached by stairs. Climbs run at dawn, day, dusk and night, and book out in peak season.

australia/the-rocks.name: The Rocks
australia/the-rocks.description: Sydney oldest quarter, with sandstone lanes, pubs, a weekend market and convict history.
australia/the-rocks.details: The Rocks sits beside Circular Quay and holds the first European settlement area. Cobbled lanes, heritage pubs, galleries and a weekend market make it easy to explore on foot. The Museum of Contemporary Art is close by.

australia/bondi-coogee-walk.name: Bondi to Coogee coastal walk
australia/bondi-coogee-walk.description: A clifftop path of about six kilometres linking Sydney best-known beaches, rock pools and sculptures.
australia/bondi-coogee-walk.details: The coastal walk runs past Tamarama, Bronte and Clovelly to Coogee, with ocean pools carved into the rock. Allow two to three hours at an easy pace, with stops for swims and cafes. Bring sun protection, as there is little shade.

australia/manly-ferry.name: Manly ferry and beach
australia/manly-ferry.description: A half-hour ferry ride across the harbour to a surf beach and village promenade.
australia/manly-ferry.details: The Manly ferry is a cheap way to see the harbour, passing the Opera House and Bridge. Manly has a long beach, a pedestrian corso and a coastal walk to Shelly Beach for snorkelling. Ferries are frequent, and the ride is part of the fun.

australia/blue-mountains.name: Blue Mountains and Three Sisters
australia/blue-mountains.description: Eucalypt-covered sandstone cliffs and valleys west of Sydney, with lookouts, waterfalls and bush walks.
australia/blue-mountains.details: The Blue Mountains is a World Heritage area reached by train or car in about two hours. Echo Point at Katoomba looks over the Three Sisters rock formation. Scenic World runs a cableway and the steepest railway in the world, and walks such as the Grand Cliff Top or Wentworth Falls vary in difficulty. The weather is cooler than Sydney.

australia/hunter-valley.name: Hunter Valley wine country
australia/hunter-valley.description: Australia oldest wine region, with cellar doors, restaurants and balloon flights two hours north of Sydney.
australia/hunter-valley.details: The Hunter Valley is known for semillon and shiraz. A tasting day by guided tour or private driver visits several cellar doors with lunch at a winery restaurant. Hot air balloon flights run at dawn. Never drive after tasting, so organise a driver.

australia/melbourne-laneways.name: Melbourne laneways and street art
australia/melbourne-laneways.description: Hidden alleys filled with street art, coffee roasters, bars and small shops in the city centre.
australia/melbourne-laneways.details: Hosier Lane, Degraves Street, Centre Place and AC/DC Lane are the heart of Melbourne laneway culture. Street art changes constantly, and the coffee is among the best in the country. Take a walking tour with a local to find hidden bars and the stories behind the art.

australia/queen-victoria-market.name: Queen Victoria Market
australia/queen-victoria-market.description: A huge open-air market with produce, deli halls, street food and Melbourne souvenirs.
australia/queen-victoria-market.details: The market has operated since 1878 and covers fresh produce, meats, cheeses, clothing and gifts. The deli hall is the best place for a snack of borek or doughnuts. It is closed on Mondays and Wednesdays, and Thursday evenings in summer have a night market.

australia/melbourne-gardens.name: Royal Botanic Gardens and the Shrine
australia/melbourne-gardens.description: A large garden with a lake and walking paths south of the river, next to the city war memorial.
australia/melbourne-gardens.details: The Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria offers shaded lawns, a lake and guided walks. The Shrine of Remembrance nearby has views over the city from its balcony. The gardens are free and an easy walk or tram ride from the centre.

australia/great-ocean-road.name: Great Ocean Road and the Twelve Apostles
australia/great-ocean-road.description: A coastal drive of limestone stacks, surf beaches and rainforest between Torquay and Warrnambool.
australia/great-ocean-road.details: The Great Ocean Road is a memorial route with Bells Beach, Lorne, Apollo Bay, the Otway rainforest and the Twelve Apostles limestone stacks. Sunset at the Apostles is the classic view, but crowds are large. A full day from Melbourne is long, about 12 hours with stops, so a guided tour is easier than driving yourself.

australia/phillip-island-penguins.name: Phillip Island penguin parade
australia/phillip-island-penguins.description: Little penguins waddle ashore at dusk on a beach about 90 minutes from Melbourne.
australia/phillip-island-penguins.details: Each evening, little penguins come ashore from the sea to their burrows at Summerland Beach. Viewing stands and a visitor centre are provided, and photography is banned to protect the birds. Dress warmly, as the wind is cold. The island also has koalas and a seal colony.

australia/yarra-valley.name: Yarra Valley wineries
australia/yarra-valley.description: Cool-climate vineyards, chocolate and cheese stops around an hour east of Melbourne.
australia/yarra-valley.details: The Yarra Valley is known for pinot noir, chardonnay and sparkling wine, and tastings are matched with produce from the area. Many tours leave from Melbourne. Hot air balloons float over the valley at sunrise. A designated driver or tour is essential.

australia/great-barrier-reef.name: Great Barrier Reef day trip
australia/great-barrier-reef.description: A boat day from Cairns or Port Douglas for snorkelling or diving on the outer reef.
australia/great-barrier-reef.details: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral system in the world. Day boats leave Cairns and Port Douglas for outer reef pontoons with snorkelling, glass-bottom boats and introductory dives. The water is clearest in the dry season, from June to October. Stinger suits are required from about November to May. Book an eco-certified operator.

australia/daintree-rainforest.name: Daintree Rainforest and Cape Tribulation
australia/daintree-rainforest.description: One of the oldest rainforests on earth, explored on boardwalks, river cruises and beach walks.
australia/daintree-rainforest.details: The Daintree is more than 100 million years old and meets the reef at Cape Tribulation. Guided tours take in Mossman Gorge, a Daintree River crocodile cruise and the Marrdja boardwalk. A cassowary may be seen, but give it space. Wet-season rain can flood roads from December to March.

australia/kuranda.name: Kuranda Scenic Railway and Skyrail
australia/kuranda.description: A heritage train through rainforest gorges to a village, returning by cable car over the canopy.
australia/kuranda.details: Kuranda is a hillside village in the rainforest above Cairns. The Scenic Railway climbs past Barron Falls through 15 tunnels and the Skyrail returns by gondola above the canopy. The village has a market, a butterfly sanctuary and a wildlife park. Allow most of a day.

australia/uluru-base-walk.name: Uluru sunrise and base walk
australia/uluru-base-walk.description: A walk around the base of the sandstone monolith, sacred to the Anangu people.
australia/uluru-base-walk.details: Uluru is a sacred site for the Anangu, and the climb has been closed since 2019. The base walk is about 10 kilometres and takes three to four hours, with the Mala and Kuniya areas explained by signs. Start early because it is very hot, and some areas ask for no photographs. The Cultural Centre explains the stories.

australia/kata-tjuta.name: Kata Tjuta and the Valley of the Winds
australia/kata-tjuta.description: A group of 36 domed rock formations 50 kilometres from Uluru, with desert walks.
australia/kata-tjuta.details: Kata Tjuta, or the Olgas, is a cluster of red conglomerate domes. The Walpa Gorge walk is short and easy, and the Valley of the Winds loop is longer and more demanding. The Valley of the Winds walk closes in extreme heat in the middle of the day. Take plenty of water.

australia/field-of-light.name: Field of Light and desert dinner
australia/field-of-light.description: A night-time installation of thousands of solar lights in the desert, or a dinner under the stars.
australia/field-of-light.details: Bruce Munro Field of Light spreads tens of thousands of glowing stems across the red sand and is walked at sunset or in the evening. Alternatives include a dinner on a dune with an astronomer. Book ahead, as seats are limited.
